first.rationale: The two observed declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the funnel itself, not at price, so I am treating the competitor's entry pricing as a symptom-adjacent pressure rather than the thing to answer directly. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is the tempting reflex, but its record reports 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' with no stated retention or margin horizon; discount-acquired SMB cohorts are exactly where short-window revenue lift and sustainable qualified revenue diverge, and the primary objective is the latter. I am therefore not spending the single slot there. I chose to verify memory_31 and memory_86 because they are my intended action's entire evidence base and they may not be independent: 'signup simplification improved SMB activation' (day 12) and 'shortening onboarding improved completion and time-to-value' (day 52) could well be one experiment consolidated twice, which would mean my apparent double support is really single support. I want the archive to tell me whether these are two records or one, what the follow-up window was, and critically whether the field-cutting arm was measured on downstream lead quality. That last point is the real risk I am flagging: cutting required fields at signup can lift activation while degrading qualification data, which would raise activation and lower qualified revenue simultaneously — the exact failure mode this objective punishes. If verification shows the memories are duplicates or that qualified-revenue effects were never measured, I will drop to a guarded test or fall back to activation_messaging (memory_91), which addresses the larger of the two declines with less signup-data risk. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) and referrals (memory_57) are plausible but address neither observed decline this week. Running as a standard experiment with retention and lead-quality guardrails instrumented alongside the completion-rate metric.

final.rationale: Verification resolved my main worry favorably: exp_31 and exp_86 are two distinct confirmed experiments, not one record consolidated twice, so the support for the onboarding direction is genuinely independent rather than double-counted. It also partly retired the failure mode I flagged — exp_31 did measure qualified revenue (+4%), so field-cutting did not silently trade activation against lead quality, though it did cost 1% of 30-day retention. exp_86 is the stronger of the two for this week: completion +13% and time-to-value -2.1 days, with retention moving the right way (+3%), which is the profile I want when the objective is sustainable qualified revenue rather than a headline number. It also maps directly onto the observed -4% completion decline, and the time-to-value gain should propagate into the -6% activation decline without my having to touch signup fields at all. So I am running the shortened-onboarding arm (exp_86 pattern) and deliberately not bundling the field-cutting arm (exp_31 pattern) into the same slot — exp_31's -1% retention is small but real, and stacking both would confound the readout and put the retention drag on top of a change I cannot separately attribute. I am still declining promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73's record remains unverified, its 'strong revenue lift' has no stated retention horizon, and discount-acquired price-sensitive SMB is the cohort most likely to show revenue that does not survive contact with renewal. Residual uncertainties I am carrying rather than papering over: exp_31's result explicitly did not replicate outside SMB, so I should not assume the onboarding finding generalizes to enterprise, where memory_44 suggests sales-assist is the better path anyway; both source experiments predate the current competitive pressure, so prior effect sizes may not hold under a changed market; and neither record reports beyond 30 days, so 'sustainable' is an extrapolation. Instrumenting 30- and 90-day retention and qualified-revenue-per-account alongside completion rate, with activation_messaging (memory_91) held as the next slot if the time-to-value channel does not carry through to activation.
